name: CHAI PPM grant BOTEC, 2024
beneficiaries_note: Nothing in the model says where; the charity's main country of operation, the one its other models name most: Nigeria.
summary: Funds CHAI's team that advises governments on making their health programs work better. GiveWell's spreadsheet "CHAI PPM grant BOTEC, 2024", linked from its grant page. Every number is traced from the sheet's bottom line; calculated rows reproduce the sheet's own values.

resources.title: GiveWell grant page (clinton health access initiative chai program performance management grant october 2024)

rows.label: Total increase in value from improvement in programs influenced by PPM team (Best guess)
rows.explainer:
Calculated in the source sheet as `=(PV(B18,B9,-B17,,1))*(1-B19)`; kept as a fixed number here (text in arithmetic).

Calculation. This accounts for a 4% discount rate and the probabiity of failure.

rows.label: Grant size ($ million) (Best guess)
rows.explainer:
CHAI, Organizational Development Budget (unpublished) From the budget CHAI provided us, they expect to spend $1.3 million annually on the Program performance management team and $0.4 million annually on Talent and enabling infrastructure. We are funding these activities for three years. 

$1.3 million + $0.4 million = $1.7 million * 3 years = $5.1 million.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar, GiveDirectly (Best guess)
rows.explainer: GiveWell calculation. Changed for consistency: GiveWell's sheet used 0.0033545 units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly here. The site values cash with one shared benchmark for every model (The cash benchmark, under Data), the same figure that turns this model's multiple of cash back into units of value: where the sheet divides by it to make its multiple, the benchmark cancels in our view, so our units of value are the sheet's before it divided by cash. The evaluator view keeps 0.0033545.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years. It is the site's shared cash benchmark (The cash benchmark, under Data), the one figure every model's multiple of cash is turned into units of value with.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this grant's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
